player_context.note: Recent workload uses up to 5 starts; pitcher rates use up to 15, and opponent rates up to 40 games. Each window is limited to the prior 370 days. Model rates include fixed priors; observed averages do not. Innings are shown in thirds (5⅔ = five innings and two outs).

build.note: This market uses the simple estimate directly. The model then turns its average into the chance of each outcome, adjusted so past forecasts matched how often things happened.

trend.label: K
trend.note: Every start in the window counts equally: up to 15 for rates and the last 5 for workload.

assessment.reason: The supplied quantitative case merits consideration at plus money, without treating its model-market disagreement as validated value.
assessment.model_case: Fifteen starts and 16.57 recent outs support expected normal volume. The opponent strikeout input supports the Under direction, but the 6.45 projection barely falls below 6.5; distribution assumptions matter.
assessment.price_case: At +115, the supplied model clears break-even, whereas the six-book exact-line reference falls below it. Main-versus-alternate placement and calibration evidence are unspecified.
assessment.context_case: No supplied source verifies a prop-specific advantage. Unpublished batting order, bullpen usage and park/weather remain sensitivity checks, not identified material blockers.

qualitative_review.countercase: A longer outing or more strikeout-prone order could erase the projected Under direction.
open_checks: Review the confirmed order and any workload change.
Reconfirm price and settlement rules.

assessment.reason: Repeated low usage supports the under direction without requiring a new favorable story.
assessment.model_case: Recent receptions of zero, one and one on one to three targets sit below 2.5. Projected targets rise to 3.7, yet projected catches remain 1.8; matchup adjustments do little work. Calibration substantially reduces the raw estimate, leaving a favorable but experimentally unvalidated case.
assessment.price_case: 2.5 is the main line, with five-book exact-line coverage. +113 requires the supplied break-even, below the calibrated estimate. Market pricing favors the opposing side; broad coverage establishes disagreement, not independent model validation.
assessment.context_case: Specific route, snap and teammate-availability reporting is absent. Repeated usage supports an expected role, not confirmed health.

qualitative_review.countercase: A target-share rebound or better catch efficiency could produce three receptions.
open_checks: Review route deployment and receiving-group changes.
Reconfirm the available quote and participation settlement.
